newsitem.title: GERMANY: No Daimler comment on report Werner opposed merger.
newsitem.headline: No Daimler comment on report Werner opposed merger.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG on Friday declined comment on media reports that the head of automotive subsidiary Mercedes-Benz AG, Helmut Werner, was not prepared to sanction a merger of Mercedes with Daimler.

Two local newspapers reported on Friday that Werner rejected a proposal by Daimler chief executive Juergen Schrempp to integrate Mercedes' management into Daimler, make Werner his deputy and appoint three other Mercedes directors to the Daimler board.
One of the papers, "Stuttgarter Zeitung," cited sources within Daimler shareholder Deutsche Bank AG as saying Werner threatened to resign if Daimler and Mercedes were merged.
Daimler and Mercedes responded by issuing a brief joint statement reiterating that the group was discussing a reorganisation to make its structure more efficient.
"Insofar as the media link this with speculation about personnel, we do not comment on that as a rule," the statement said.
Sources close to Daimler on Thursday said Daimler was considering a plan under which Mercedes would be fully integrated into the parent company.

The plan is seen as part of a drive by Daimler-Benz chief Juergen Schrempp to take Daimler back to its roots as a transportation group, reversing the move by his predecessor Edzard Reuter to create an integrated technology holding group.

Following the dissolution earlier this year of its loss-making AEG industrial division and the bankruptcy of the majority-held Fokker Dutch plane-maker unit, analysts said such a move would be viewed as a logical next step.

Sources close to Daimler believe that an internal "merger" of the Mercedes-Benz car- and truck-making unit, which now makes up around three-quarters of its group revenues, would also likely be accompanied by management changes.

There has been widespread speculation that Mercedes-Benz chairman Helmut Werner, accredited with having achieved a major turnaround at the unit, opposes the plan as effectively making his position redundant.
